sources.title: Ocimum basilicum — NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
How to Grow Basil in Your Garden
sources.authors: Lindsay Pearson and Dan Drost, Utah State University Extension

passages.title: Light and growing location
passages.text: For sweet basil, choose a bright growing location. NC State Extension describes full sunlight as preferred and also lists partial shade among suitable conditions. This is garden guidance, not a calibrated indoor grow-light schedule.

passages.title: Pruning and branching
passages.text: Trim shoot tips and remove developing flower buds to encourage a more branched plant. This is general pruning guidance, not a diagnosis of a particular plant.

passages.title: Examples of pests and diseases
passages.text: The NC State guide lists aphids and Japanese beetles as possible pests and mentions fusarium wilt and downy mildew. Listing these problems does not diagnose a photographed leaf.

passages.title: Seed germination in soil
passages.text: Utah State University Extension recommends sowing outdoors after the final spring frost. Its guide gives a soil germination temperature of 75–85°F and a typical wait of 10–14 days. These are soil-germination conditions, not reservoir-temperature targets.

passages.title: Beginning the harvest
passages.text: The Utah State guide says harvesting can begin at the six-to-eight-leaf stage. Leave some foliage on the plant when cutting stems; its guidance specifies keeping two to four leaves.

passages.title: Confirmation and pump safety
passages.text: BasilCare pump requests require user confirmation and must go through the authenticated API safety checks. The Raspberry Pi also applies local cutoffs independently.

passages.title: Meaning of camera detection boxes
passages.text: BasilCare presents camera-model boxes as hints rather than a confirmed disease diagnosis. The live-camera design records model quality as a limitation of the demonstration.
